body:
## Precision on the Aspartate case

Verified in `chebi.db`, `CHEBI:132943 aspartate` is not merely "a structure-free
class" — it is the **charge-agnostic parent**, with both charge states as its
direct children:

```
CHEBI:132943  aspartate
  ├── CHEBI:29995  aspartate(2-)
  └── CHEBI:35391  aspartate(1-)
```

That is the crux, and it makes the case tighter than I first stated. Grounding
a bare label to `CHEBI:132943` is not a *different* reading of the convention;
it **under-specifies relative to the parent/child structure**, landing on a node
that deliberately refuses to commit to a protonation state — while the sibling
record `Glutamate` sits on `CHEBI:29987 glutamate(2-)`, one level down.

Two consequences worth recording:

- The move `CHEBI:132943 → CHEBI:29995` adds **no stereochemical claim**: both
  terms are stereo-agnostic (neither is L- nor D-specific), so the only thing
  that changes is protonation specificity. That removes the main objection to
  making the change.
- `aspartate` is also a *synonym* of `CHEBI:29995`, so the lexical evidence that
  justified the original mapping survives the correction intact.

This also sharpens what the documented rule needs to say: the test is not "is
there an `X(n-)` term" but "**is the current target a charge-agnostic parent
that has `X(n-)` children**". `Ascorbate` passes the check by the same test for
the opposite reason — `CHEBI:22651`'s only child is `L-ascorbate`, a
*stereochemical* refinement rather than a protonation one, so there is no
deprotonated child to descend to.

## Correction: I overstated this. §3 documents the general rule.

I claimed the convention is "written down nowhere". That is wrong.
`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 "Identity granularity — one record per substance"
contains an **ordered decision procedure** that governs exactly this class of
choice, and my search missed it because I grepped for the phrases the *evidence
notes* use (`bare anion`, `fully deprotonated`) rather than reading the document.

§3 step 4 is the relevant rule and it generalises the case correctly:

> **The label is genuinely under-specified and an unspecified-sense parent term
> exists** — *and the record carries no independent evidence of which specific
> sense it is*. Then the label denotes the unspecified sense: use that term with
> `exactMatch`, and do not reach for a specific child.
>
> **The evidence escape hatch is the point, not an exception.** … A short label
> does not override record-level evidence.

That is a better-stated version of what I proposed writing, and it already
covers `Ascorbate` (stay at the parent) and the `Arabitol` precedent.

## The narrower gap that does stand

§3's axis is **sense/specificity** — hydration, salt form, stereochemistry,
locants. It does **not** address **protonation state** anywhere: the words
anion, cation, protonation, charge and conjugate do not appear in the document.
Two consequences remain unresolved by it:

1. **Does a bare anion label descend to `X(n-)`?** `Aspartate` on the
   charge-agnostic parent `CHEBI:132943` (children `aspartate(2-)` and
   `aspartate(1-)`) is arguably step 4 — under-specified label, unspecified-sense
   parent, stay put — yet the sibling `Glutamate` sits on `glutamate(2-)`, and
   the growth-medium-pH argument is a *chemical* reason to descend that step 4
   does not contemplate. The data is inconsistent either way, so one reading
   needs to be chosen and written down.

2. **For a salt, is the `narrowMatch` parent the acid or the anion?** This
   recurs on every `… sodium salt` record. §3's own hypophosphite example
   anchors to the salt rather than stripping to the acid, which suggests the
   anion, but it is not stated.

So the fix is much smaller than I proposed: **add a protonation/charge clause to
the existing §3 procedure**, not document a convention from scratch. The
Aspartate/Ascorbate/Protocatechuate/2-dehydro-D-gluconate set is still the right
worked example — four bare-anion labels with four different correct resolutions.

Surfaced by a research agent that read §3 and applied it as the standard, which
is also the answer to the "where is this written down" question I raised on its
behalf.

## The cohort is 5, not 6 — `Quinate` was a false positive

My cohort detector matched charged children with `\(\d?[-+]\)`, which also
matches the **stereodescriptor** in `(-)-quinate`. `CHEBI:26490 quinate`'s
children are:

```
(-)-quinate              <- a stereochemical refinement, not a protonation state
1,3-dicaffeoylquinate    <- a derivative
```

Neither is an `X(n-)` charge state, so `Quinate` is not in this population at
all. It is the `Ascorbate` situation: the only child refines something other
than protonation, so there is nothing to descend to.

The real cohort, verified against `chebi.db` children:

| record | parent | charged children | occurrences |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Malate` | CHEBI:25115 | `malate(2-)` | 0 |
| `Succinate` | CHEBI:26806 | `succinate(2-)`, `succinate(1-)` | 0 |
| `Azelaate` | CHEBI:132955 | `azelaate(2-)` | 13 |
| `Glutarate` | CHEBI:24329 | `glutarate(2-)`, `glutarate(1-)` | 1 |
| `Oxalate` | CHEBI:132952 | `oxalate(2-)`, `oxalate(1-)` | 2 |

Note `Succinate` carries a caution from the research lane — that `CHEBI:26806`
is *genuinely* protonation-agnostic ("at least one carboxy group") rather than
merely unspecified, which would make descending it wrong. I could not confirm
that from `chebi.db`: the term has **no definition** there, and neither do the
other four. So the distinction the lane drew is not checkable from the local
build and needs the live ChEBI entry.

That matters for the policy: the rule cannot be "descend whenever charged
children exist", because at least one of these five may be a deliberate
protonation-agnostic class rather than an under-specified one, and the local
data cannot tell them apart.

## Resolved — with live ChEBI definitions the local build does not carry

The blocker was real: `chebi.db` has **no definitions**, so the
deliberately-agnostic vs merely-unspecified distinction could not be made
offline. Fetched live from OLS4, and all five hold-outs read identically:

> "A dicarboxylic acid anion obtained by deprotonation of **at least one** of the
> carboxy groups of *X* acid."

`malate` · `succinate` · `azelaate` · `glutarate` · `oxalate` — every one.

That is a **deliberately protonation-agnostic class**: it already spans the mono-
and di-anion, so a bare label belongs on it. **All five correctly stay where they
are.** The research lane's caution about `Succinate` was right, and it
generalises to the whole cohort.

## And it vindicates the Aspartate change on better evidence

`CHEBI:132943 aspartate` carries **no definition at all**, even live. Nothing
asserts it is deliberately agnostic, so it is merely unspecified — and the
sibling precedent (`Glutamate` on `CHEBI:29987 glutamate(2-)`) decides it. The
descent applied earlier stands, now on firmer ground than when it was made: at
the time the argument was precedent plus pH; now there is a positive test that
separates it from the five.

## The rule, written into §3

> Read the parent term's definition. **"At least one"** → deliberately agnostic →
> **stay**. No such definition, and `X(n-)` children exist → merely unspecified →
> **descend** to the species present at growth-medium pH.

Documented with the worked table covering both outcomes, the `Ascorbate` and
`Protocatechuate` cases where there is nothing to descend to, the explicit
caveat that the test cannot be applied offline, and the salt-parent convention
from #322 (the narrowMatch parent follows the label, which sidesteps acid-vs-anion).

No data changes — the five were already correct. Closing once the docs PR lands.

Resolved and documented in #339. All five hold-outs carry an explicit "at least one" definition and correctly stay put; `Aspartate` has no definition and correctly descended. The rule and its offline caveat are now in MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3.

## Live ChEBI definitions for the #320 protonation/oxidation group

This issue notes the local ChEBI build lacks definitions for some of these terms. Read from the **live EBI OLS4 API** instead, here is the whole group — and applying this issue's own rule ("*deprotonation of **at least one***" = deliberately agnostic → stay; specific or absent → descend) settles most of them without a new policy.

| record | term | live definition | verdict under #319's rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Malate` | `CHEBI:25115` malate | "deprotonation of **at least one** of the carboxy groups of malic acid" | **stay** — agnostic, exactly the five hold-outs' wording |
| `3-Hydroxypropionate` | `CHEBI:16510` | "the conjugate base of 3-hydroxypropionic acid" | **stay** — the *label* names the anion, so no protonation question arises |
| `DL-carnitine` | `CHEBI:17126` carnitine | structural ("an amino-acid betaine that is butanoate substituted…") — says nothing about protonation | **stay** — the CAS pointing at `carnitinium` doesn't make the neutral term wrong |
| `phosphorous acid` | `CHEBI:36361` | **no definition** | **stay** — label matches the term label exactly; the CAS's "phosphonic acid" is the IUPAC name for the same compound, a naming variant not an error |
| `EDTA` | `CHEBI:64755` EDTA(2-) | "deprotonation of **two of the four** carboxy groups" | **descend** — *specific*, not agnostic; the label asserts no charge state |
| `Cobalamine` | `CHEBI:28911` cob(III)alamin | "oxidation state of **+3**" | **descend** — done in #350 → `CHEBI:30411 cobalamin` |
| `Thiamine pyrophosphate` | `CHEBI:18290` | "an organic **chloride salt** of thiamine(1+) diphosphate" | **descend** — the label says nothing about chloride |
| `0.2% Thiamine pyrophosphate` | `CHEBI:9532` | matches TPP | **stay** — its CAS `154-87-0` is the chloride's, so the CAS is the wrong field |

So **4 of 8 need no change at all** — they're the same benign pattern as this issue's five hold-outs — and only 3 genuinely descend.

## Two need a decision I did not take

**`EDTA`** (occ **446**) should come off `EDTA(2-)`, but `CHEBI:4735 ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid` is held by `EDTA (acid form)` — a record with **0 occurrences**. Merging the 446-occurrence record into an unused one is backwards, and the existence of an explicit "(acid form)" label suggests the corpus means to distinguish them. Options: merge anyway (winner keeps `EDTA`'s label), mint a protonation-agnostic identifier for `EDTA` per §3 step 3, or retire the empty acid-form record and give `EDTA` the term.

**`Thiamine pyrophosphate`** (occ 17) should move to `CHEBI:9532`, but that is held by `0.2% Thiamine pyrophosphate` (occ 1) — a **stock solution**, not the pure compound. #288's precedent mints `kgmicrobe.ingredient:` for stock solutions, which would free the term for the pure compound. That is the likely right answer but it changes a record #288 already settled, so it should be confirmed rather than assumed.

Both are recorded here rather than guessed at. Everything else in the group is either resolved or verified as needing no change.
